parsed.explanation: A transgender visitor is exposed to a state that treats trans visibility itself as criminal material: depictions of trans people are classed as pornography (Art. 343, up to four years; thirteen with minors), and a 2026 law bans 'propaganda of gender reassignment'. Enforcement is documented and immediate — an arrest wave with eight trans people detained in one month, beatings, coerced charges, custody abuse, and prisons where staff encourage abuse of sexual minorities. There is no anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime recording, no asylum ground, no regional court, and police collect passport data and photographs of LGBT people. Public opinion is heavily hostile and state media equates LGBTI with paedophilia. No capital charge for presentation is documented, placing this above the execution-tier anchors but firmly in the arrest-and-custody-abuse tier.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented precedent: in 2004 authorities threatened immediate expulsion of foreigners attending LGBT workshops under an 'intervention in domestic affairs' article. Marker-mismatch handling at the border is not documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Attendance at any LGBT-connected event converts a routine visit into an expulsion or Article 343 exposure; ordinary crossings' document practice is unstated.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: 15+ LGBT people detained in September 2024, eight transgender, charged with hooliganism and pornography; physical and psychological abuse in custody; coerced charges; beatings at arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Custody blackmail/extortion and staff-encouraged prisoner abuse reported.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Discovery escalates from identification to charge to custody, where trans detainees are unprotected and abuse is corroborated rather than remedied.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prisons: homosexuality subject to speculation, blackmail and extortion; staff often encourage other prisoners to abuse sexual minorities. Venues declined, raided or closed; riot-police raids on pride events.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Unitary state, no subnational variation documented; police and prison institutions are themselves the exposure.

care_services.exposure: Qualified psychological help generally unavailable; no transgender-specific facilities documented. Care denial or medication seizure for visitors not documented.
care_services.interaction: No documented care pathway for trans visitors; emergency or hormonal need would be handled without any identity-respecting protocol.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: trans depiction classed as pornography alongside paedophilia and necrophilia; 2026 ban on 'propaganda of gender reassignment'; planned administrative 'LGBTI propaganda' penalties; state TV equating LGBTI with paedophilia and foreign weapons; 'traditional values' security concept.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Not documented. Constitutional equality guarantee has not operated in practice.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The statute frames trans presence as harm to children, licensing police to charge visibility, not conduct, and enabling escalation where minors are involved.

minors_guardians.exposure: Penalty for the pornography offence rises to thirteen years where children are involved; propaganda law bundles gender reassignment with childlessness and paedophilia. Treatment of a trans minor or accompanying guardian is not otherwise documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family travelling with a trans minor faces the harshest charging tier on the same depiction rationale; a guardian's exposure rises with the child's visibility.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: police beat LGBT people during arrest and charging; brutality against sexual minorities not registered or investigated; officers collect passport details and photographs at cruising areas in two cities; unprovoked bar raids. Two trans men raped in 2008 did not report, doubting police would help.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime prohibition, no published hate-crime data, no national reporting contact since 2015.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State actors are perpetrators or bystanders; recourse is absent, so reporting an assault invites further exposure rather than remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection, no SOGI asylum ground, no hate-crime law, no regional human-rights court membership; clear legal and political climate with arbitrary detention and retained death penalty.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented. Civil-society submissions are the only data source.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absent any forum, an outed visitor has no route to challenge expulsion, charge or abuse; whether the 2026 law reaches foreigners and how border officers treat foreign markers are unanswered.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vesskaria documents executions and capital prosecutions for presentation. Here the penalty ceiling is four years (thirteen with minors) with custody abuse and beatings but no documented capital charge or killing for gender presentation, so this dossier sits clearly higher, though the arrest-to-abuse chain is comparable.

Oskara's morality sweeps, coerced statements, custody violence and failing courts closely match this dossier's arrest wave, coerced charges and prison abuse. Slightly higher here because the statutory penalty is explicit and charged (pornography, hooliganism) while Oskara's capital clause is doubtful, but both remain in the same tier.

Ostravia's reporting-and-eviction regime ends in fines and lost lodging, with no imprisonment. This jurisdiction arrests, charges and beats those it identifies, so it is materially below that anchor; exclusion there is a ceiling, here it is a floor.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is one in which the state itself produces the exposure. Trans visibility is defined as pornographic material, advocacy of transition is banned, and police document, arrest and charge LGBT people, including a recent wave detaining eight transgender individuals, with beatings and coerced confessions corroborated by civil society. Prisons offer no protection and staff encourage abuse. No anti-discrimination, hate-crime, asylum or regional-court remedy exists, so discovery carries no counterweight. Against this, the dossier establishes no capital application to gender presentation and no border-marker procedure, leaving the visitor's fate after discovery in the arrest-and-custody tier rather than the execution tier — but with severity-4 custody abuse documented and near-certain hostility from both police and public.
